draft.title: The three economic questions
card: Resources are scarce, so every society must answer three questions about how to use them.
which goods and services to make, and how much of each.
which resources and methods to use, such as people's work or machines.
how the goods and services made are shared among the people.
draft.remember: Every society must decide what, how and who.

a.q: A government decides to use its land and workers to build homes, not a golf course. Which question is it answering?
a.why: The choice is about which goods and services to make, so it answers what to produce. It is not how to produce, which is about the methods used to build them.
a.clue: The choice is about which thing to make.

b.q: Sam's bakery in Geelong swaps hand kneading for a dough machine. Which question is Sam answering?
b.why: Sam is choosing a method, using a machine in place of people's work. That is how to produce. The bakery still makes bread, so what to produce has not changed.
b.clue: Look at what changed: the product or the method?
